reference: The ball which the dog fetched is now completely covered in mud.
sk: Lopta, ktorú pes priniesol, je teraz úplne od blata.
cz: Míček, který pes přinesl, je teď úplně od bláta.
acceptable: The ball {which|that|} the dog {fetched|brought back|brought} is {now |}{completely|totally} covered {in|with} mud.
The ball {which|that|} the dog {fetched|brought back|brought} is {completely|totally} covered {in|with} mud now.
The ball {which|that|} the dog {fetched|brought back|brought} is {now |}{completely|totally} muddy.

mistakes.text: The ball {which|that} the dog {fetched|brought} it is now completely covered in mud.
mistakes.feedback_sk: V Relative clause sa predmet neopakuje: bez „it“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: V Relative clause se předmět neopakuje: bez „it“.
mistakes.feedback_en: Don't repeat the object in a Relative clause: “which/that” already replaces “it”.

mistakes.text: The ball {who|what} the dog {fetched|brought} is now completely covered in mud.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Pre veci patrí „which“ alebo „that“; „who“ je pre ľudí a „what“ sem nepatrí.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Pro věci se používá „which“ nebo „that“; „who“ je pro lidi a „what“ sem nepatří.
mistakes.feedback_en: For things use “which” or “that”; “who” is for people and “what” doesn't work here.

mistakes.text: The ball {which|that} {fetched|brought} the dog is now completely covered in mud.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Takto lopta priniesla psa. Podmet ide pred sloveso: „which the dog fetched“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Takhle míček přinesl psa. Podmět jde před sloveso: „which the dog fetched“.
mistakes.feedback_en: This means the ball fetched the dog. Put the subject before the verb: “which the dog fetched”.

mistakes.text: The ball {which|that|} the dog {fetched|brought} is now completely from mud.
mistakes.feedback_sk: „Od blata“ sa neprekladá doslova: povedz „covered in mud“ alebo „muddy“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: „Od bláta“ se nepřekládá doslova: řekni „covered in mud“ nebo „muddy“.
mistakes.feedback_en: Don't translate word for word: say “covered in mud” or “muddy”.
